summary: Wooden 100-ft Lyells tower completed 1938 (1955 item says 1937 with CCC labor); pulled down 11 July 1955; lookout list marks it gone; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Wooden tower of creosoted pine timber
facts.status_note: Pulled down on 11 July 1955 per a 1955 item; the lookout list marks it gone; no source describes the site now

access.note: A 1955 item places the tower on a private farm; no source says who owns the land now or whether it is open to visitors

events.note: July 1, 1938 item reports construction completed as a 100-foot tower; a 1955 item instead says it was built in 1937 with C.C.C. labor
Pulled down on Monday, July 11, 1955, per the 1955 item; a steel replacement was planned

evidence.supports: July 1938 item: State Conservation Commission completed a 100-foot tower at Lyells, Richmond County
evidence.quote: The State Conservation Commission has completed construction of a 100-foot lookout tower at Lyells, Richmond County, Route 3.

evidence.supports: 1955 item: tower built in 1937 with C.C.C. labor
evidence.quote: The tower was built in 1937 with C.C.C. labor.
The timber used in the tower was creosoted pine
It stood 120 feet tall, higher than any of the other fire towers in the Tappahannock District.

evidence.supports: view on a clear day of the Rappahannock and Potomac Rivers
evidence.quote: On a clear day, both the Rappahannock and Potomac Rivers were visible from this tower.

evidence.supports: tower stood on a farm (Bert Edwards)
evidence.quote: on the farm of Bert Edwards

evidence.supports: 1955 item places the tower in Westmoreland County
evidence.quote: This tower was located at Lyells, Virginia in Westmoreland County

evidence.supports: last four wooden towers in Virginia; this was the only one in Tidewater Virginia
evidence.quote: The last four wooden forest fire towers in the State of Virginia are being replaced this summer by steel towers.

evidence.supports: only one of the last four wooden towers in Tidewater Virginia
evidence.quote: The only one of these in Tidewater Virginia, was pulled down Monday July 11.

evidence.supports: steel tower planned to replace the wooden one
evidence.quote: Plans are already underway to replace the wooden tower with a new steel one.

evidence.supports: steel replacement planned; construction in August by the Virginia Forest Service
evidence.quote: construction work being done in August, by the Virginia Forest Service

evidence.supports: lookout list entry Lyells (Westmoreland): coordinates 38.00428, -76.73299; status Gone
Wikipedia places Lyells in Richmond County
evidence.quote: Lyells is an unincorporated community in Richmond County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1938 item says 100 feet; the 1955 item says the tower stood 120 feet. Kept 30.5 m (100 ft) from the 1938 completion report, which was written when the tower was new. The 1955 figure is a later recollection.

The 1938 item reports completion in July 1938; the 1955 item says the tower was built in 1937 with C.C.C. labor. Recorded 1938 as the year of the completion report and kept the 1937 claim in the note.

The lookout list and the Forest Lookouts header say Westmoreland County; the 1938 item and Wikipedia say Richmond County. Not resolved from these sources. The record keeps Westmoreland, which matches the list name, and the story says the sources disagree.

The page header says Virginia Division of Forestry; the 1938 item names the State Conservation Commission and the 1955 item names the Virginia Forest Service. Kept the record's agency name, which matches the page header.

sources.title: Lyells (Westmoreland), Forest Lookouts (quoting Northern Neck News, 1938 and 1955)
Virginia, Forest Fire Lookout Association lookout list

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: county (Westmoreland per list and 1955 item; Richmond per 1938 item and Wikipedia). Height: 100 ft (1938) vs 120 ft (1955); the record keeps 30.5 m. Year of construction: 1937 vs 1938. The planned steel replacement is not confirmed by any source read. Access level 'private' rests only on the 1955 farm description. No site-today source found; no new photos found; no staffing or fire sources in these pages.
